messages:
deploy-bot: Initiating canary rollout: runtime-v2.3.1 -> 10% (us-west1). Plan: +10% every 10m to 50%. Change window 11:00-12:00 PT. Release notes: fix KV cache thrash, batching backpressure, kernel selection tweak. CI: green. Link: https://ci.redwood/release/2.3.1
jamie: Ack, watching metrics. Will call stop/go on any SLO regressions. cc @zara @rick
sam: quick heads-up — the kernel tweak touches async allocator path. Smoke tests passed but watch OOM/latency p95.
zara: Oncall standing by. Dashboard link: https://dash.redwood/canary/runtime-v2.3.1
ci-bot: Canary healthcheck: all probes OK at t+2m.
deploy-bot: Canary progressed to 10% (33 hosts). Next step scheduled in 8m.
incidents-bot: ALERT: p95 latency for /v1/generate increased to 980ms (> 750ms threshold) in us-west1 at 1763512380.
jamie: seeing that spike. Any 500s?
rick: small bump in 5xxs (0.7% -> 1.8%) from worker-7 pool. Investigating logs.
sam: grabbing logs now. If it's allocator OOMs we should hold.
ci-bot: Recent deploys: runtime-v2.3.1 -> commit abc123. Previous stable: runtime-v2.3.0 (commit 9f8e7).
sam: logs show repeated allocation failure in worker-7: "failed to allocate kv-cache: out of memory". Pattern started right after v2.3.1 started accepting long-context requests.
jamie: Hold the rollout. Do NOT increase percent. Pause scheduled. @deploy-bot please acknowledge manual pause. :warning:
deploy-bot: Rollout paused by jamie at 1763512405. Remaining scheduled steps cancelled.
arlene: Any customer-facing impact? We have one high-traffic tenant in us-west1.
rick: Small error rate increase for that tenant (1 of 120 requests sampled failed). No escalations yet. I can pin that tenant's route back to v2.3.0 while we debug.
jamie: Yes pin them. Share pin command.
rick: Run in router: 
```
# pin customer route to stable runtime
curl -X POST https://router.redwood/api/pin \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ROUTER_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"tenant_id":"acme-corp","target":"runtime-v2.3.0"}'
```
Done once I run it.
sam: For immediate mitigation, scale down kv-cache size or revert allocator change. Which is quicker?
jamie: Pin + smaller kv-cache as hotfix. Sam, can you prepare a 2.3.1-hotfix branch with kv-cache reverted? We'll test on canary hosts.
sam: On it. Will publish a hotfix image in ~20m.
deploy-bot: Noted: rollout paused; manual resume required.
jamie: Thanks. Post-plan: pin acme-corp, hold public rollout, create rollback/hotfix PR, test on a subset of canary hosts, then decide stop/go.
arlene: I'll notify CS about a possible brief edge-case for the tenant. No need to page customers yet.
zara: I'll keep paging channel open and will escalate if error rate >3% or p95 >1s.
ci-bot: Smoke after pin: acme-corp traffic routed to runtime-v2.3.0 at 1763512480.
rick: Pin applied. Monitoring for regressions.
sam: Built hotfix image (runtime-v2.3.1-kvfix-1) and pushed to staging registry. Running quick functional tests.
ci-bot: Staging tests pass for hotfix image at 1763512545.
jamie: Good. Plan B if hotfix fails: full rollback to 2.3.0 and re-run release gating with smaller kernel change. For now, keep rollout paused.
arlene: Can we capture learnings and draft a short blameless note for the release channel after we stabilize?
jamie: Yes — we'll post an incident note if we escalate. For now: HOLD (no resume). :thumbsup:
ci-bot: Thread closed for rollout actions; follow-up PR links will be posted in this thread.
